edge_explainer: Unity's last quarter shows a 30.8% gross margin against 73.8% a year earlier, which looks like a collapse and is not one: a $270.5 million intangible impairment from the advertising-business exit, pre-announced a month before quarter-end and tagged discretely in the filing. That is honest disclosure of a real write-down, so there is nothing to exclude here. What is left is a fair price. Prob-weighted fair value lands within a dollar of spot and the street's target is 7% above — this is fairly-paid risk with the edge overlay simply absent. The one genuinely attractive feature is what the tape shows: Unity rose 11% during the seven weeks the semiconductor equipment complex fell between 13% and 36%, so like UiPath it diversifies rather than compounds a book already 26% AI-complex. But the entire thesis is whether the Vector rebuild recaptures ad share at a higher take rate after deliberately shedding low-quality revenue, and that is unobservable in the filings — no disclosed share, eCPM or match-rate metric exists. It resolves on August 6th, three days from now, in the exact print that re-bases the model. Entering before it is a blind bet; waiting costs nothing.
